spec.world: Third-person action game, camera following just behind and above the rider the whole time. A young Black Ethiopian man in his twenties gallops a grey horse across a vast desert of red sand and black volcanic rock in the medieval Ethiopian highlands, around the twelfth century. He wears a white cotton shamma cloak with a woven red border flying behind him, a white head wrap, a leather round shield and a long spear. Ahead, a salt caravan of camels led by Black Ethiopian men in white cotton, a small rock-hewn stone church and round thatched huts on a ridge. Straight ahead a colossal red sandstorm, a haboob wall of dust hundreds of metres high, rolls toward him and is about to swallow the desert. Golden afternoon, wide Leone landscape, dust from the hooves, fine grain.
beats: The colossal sandstorm crashes over the caravan and races at the rider; the dust wall swallows the camels one by one.
The rider gallops into the sandstorm: swirling red dust fills the entire frame, the sun is gone, only his white cloak shows in the orange haze.
Deep inside the storm the dust glows; tall shining shapes loom faintly through it ahead of the rider.

The sandstorm thins and blows past behind the rider. The dust clears to reveal the far future: gleaming silver towers, glass domes over a green oasis city, fields of solar mirrors, a train gliding on tall pylons across the plain.

Clear bright sky now. The rider on his grey horse gallops toward an Afrofuturist Ethiopian city: white and copper towers carved like rock-hewn churches, banners woven with tibeb patterns, green terraces with water channels.
Black Ethiopian people in white cotton and silver cloth wave from the terraces as the rider arrives; drones carry water over the green fields.
